title: Split the test suite into categories so review rounds don't each need a full gate, and resource-sensitive tests stop failing under load
outcome:
Greg, 2026-10-01 about 21:15Z, in Termal::Fable2's session: "should we split tests into categories? I understand, now we run full suite, right?" Then, on the coordinator's proposal: "przekaz architektom. to jest problem" (pass it to the architects; this is a problem).

Today every change runs the full five-stage gate (about 13–17 minutes: cargo-check, typescript, fingerprint tests, about 3,200 Rust tests, about 4,400 Vitest tests), and every review round with a correction needs another full gate on the exact input. On 2026-10-01 the P0 (w-1b692f268123) needed several full gates and w-e57a7f7e8da0 five. Two gate failures today came from load, not from the change:
- VirtualizedConversationMessageList "tall rehydrate": 4.4 s standalone, more than 10 s in the full run (test-9738f651);
- the git-fixture setup failures in test-47c8cb36 (w-0df837639307).

Proposal for the architects to decide and refine:
(1) Categories: fast deterministic unit tests; integration tests (git fixtures, Engram processes, real SQLite writers); slow or timing-sensitive tests in a separate serialized lane.
(2) Process: during review rounds, the fast category plus the tests affected by the change; one full gate at the end, on the exact frozen input, before the commit. The rule "full gate green on exactly what is committed" stays unchanged; only the order changes. That is a change to authority text (review-changes.md and the commit-and-push section), so it lands only through (a), (b) and (c), and only as a reordering, not a loosening.
(3) A budget: any test above a set duration (for example 2 s) is flagged for repair automatically, never by raising timeouts.
Owners: Termal::Architect2 leads the design (launcher, Rust, process); Termal::Architect1 owns the Vitest/UI categorization. Implementation is assigned after the decision.
acceptance: Any change to review-changes.md or the commit-and-push section lands only through the authority-text path (both coordinators' concurrence on the exact wording, Greg sent the wording, and the final-diff audit recorded), and keeps the full gate on the exact committed input.
Tests above the duration budget are reported by name in the launcher's summary; no timeout is raised to meet the budget.

The architects' decision is recorded as a note: the categories, how each test is assigned, the lane each runs in, and what runs per review round versus at the final freeze, with measured durations from recent full runs as evidence.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree; its run directory and fingerprint are cited in a note.

The launcher supports running a category on its own, and the full gate runs every category, with resource-sensitive tests in a serialized lane; a test covers category selection and the serialized lane.
